summary: Josephine County lookout on King Mountain (once Onion Springs Mountain), 1931 to 1972; a 1953 windstorm blew down the tower and the site's current state is not described in any source.

facts.design: Tower with live-in cab; FFLOS gives a 1931 50-ft pole platform with camp, then 50-ft and 40-ft live-in towers
facts.status_note: Removed 1972 per FFLOS, destroyed 1972 per firelookout.com; no source describes what remains at the site today

events.note: Cooperative tower and cabin on Onion Springs Mountain reported complete (June 1930 Forest Log item); a December 1930 item says the name was officially changed to King's Butte
Lightning started three more fires on the mountain in August 1930, on top of four earlier ones
First lookout on the site: FFLOS and firelookout.com give a 50-ft pole platform with camp; a June 1931 newspaper item gives a 40-ft tower with a small cabin
Roy Edwards in charge; he and his wife lived in a small cabin at the base of the tower
June 1931 item: King Mountain to replace Onion Springs on the maps, in honor of assistant state forester Porter S. King
Station placed in service June 15, 1932 with Roy Edwards in charge for a second season
FFLOS and firelookout.com: a 50-ft live-in tower replaced the first lookout in 1936. The newspaper records say the CCC started a 54-ft tower in July 1936
CCC-built 50-ft timber tower with a 14 x 14 cabin; construction completed March 17, 1939 (per the page's annual report entries)
Army post on the mountain, called AWS in the records, activated October 10, 1942 and linked to the Roseburg Filter Center; deactivated October 16, 1943
52-ft tower blown down and demolished in a January 1953 windstorm (Oregonian item); the Forest Log calls it a total loss
FFLOS and firelookout.com give a 40-ft live-in tower in 1953. No source found confirms this year for the replacement
Unmanned Air Force radar site activated; Gap Filler building and fuel tank installed
Air Force declared the site excess property on May 13; transferred to BLM in September

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1930 newspaper item reports a tower and cabin completed on Onion Springs Mountain by June 1930; FFLOS and firelookout.com give 1931 and a 50-ft pole platform, while the 1931 newspaper gives a 40-ft tower. The story gives 1931 as the register date and describes the 1930 and 1931 reports; the Weebly page's township (33S-5W-24) and elevation (5,242 ft) are close to the register's entry (5,265 ft), which supports treating them as one peak.

The newspaper reports a 52-ft tower blown down and demolished in January 1953; the register says a 40-ft live-in tower replaced the lookout in 1953. The story reports both. No source found confirms when the 40-ft tower went up.

notes_for_editor: The Weebly page carries 1930 to 1965 newspaper items and annual report entries. Its items disagree with the register on the 1931 date and tower type (40-ft tower vs 50-ft pole platform), the 1936 tower (54 ft started, 50 ft completed 1939, vs 50 ft in 1936), and the 1953 tower (52 ft blown down vs a 40-ft replacement). The Weebly page also uses the name King Mountain for August 1930 before the June 1931 map renaming; a December 1930 item reports an official change to King's Butte. Its 1958 Air Force radar entry may be about a separate facility on the same peak. Elevation: FFLOS gives 1,605 m (5,265 ft); the newspaper gives 5,242 ft. No source describes the site today, and nothing in the sources says whether the public can reach it, so no access key is included. Original newspapers were not checked. Naming: the story now uses King Mountain, the 1931 map name; the register and the hiking guide spell it Kings.
